Phantom is on a mission to connect the world to the freedom of open markets. Tens of millions of people all over the world use Phantom to access global markets that never close, including perpetuals, prediction markets, tokenized assets, stablecoins and memes. Phantom users are able to discover the markets that matter and the cultural moments that shape them, building conviction through real-time data and the verified performance of top traders. With self-custody and access to open networks at its core, Phantom lets them control their financial moves in the same app they use to safely store or spend money worldwide.

Phantom has reached #1 in Google Play's finance category and consistently ranks in the top 50 apps across all categories. Check out our Forbes Fintech 50 and CNBC and Statista's World's Top Fintech Companies 2026!

We are around 180 people, fully remote, backed by a $150M Series C investment from a16z, Sequoia Capital and Paradigm.

Responsibilities

  • Feature development: You will be owning features on our web platforms – currently the Phantom Extension and our website.

  • New initiatives and products: You will be leading initiatives to add support for other blockchains to Phantom, and to launch new complementary products or infrastructure.

  • Interfacing with users: You will be interfacing directly with end-users and developers building on Phantom – supporting them and collecting feedback to inform the direction of the product.

  • Team building: You will be working with the team to create and foster a culture of raising the bar with each new hire.

Qualifications

  • Bachelors degree in Computer Science or related technical field or equivalent practical experience

  • 5+ years full-time software engineering experience with some of the following technologies:

    • React / Typescript / React-Query

    • Solana web3.js / ethers.js

  • Demonstrated interest in open and community-driven platforms

  • English language proficiency

  • Nice-To-Have: experience in a blockchain based project

The target base salary for this role will range between $180,000 to $220,000 with the addition of equity and benefits. This is determined by a few factors including your skillset, prior relevant experience, quality of interviews and market factors (such as location) at the point in time of offer.

Why Work With Us

Phantom's journey to becoming a global trading app began with making crypto easier to use. Today, we’re building on that foundation to help people discover the markets that matter, make informed financial moves, and safely store or spend their money worldwide. Joining Phantom means helping shape that next chapter: building products that bring the freedom of open markets to more people.

 

  • Build for global impact: Create products used by tens of millions of people, making innovative financial markets more accessible to users around the world.

  • Make complexity feel simple: Solve meaningful challenges across design, engineering, and user experience to make discovering markets and managing money seamless.

  • Put users in control: Help build a future where people have greater freedom over their assets and financial decisions, with security and self-custody at the foundation.

As a Senior Data Engineer at Phantom, you’ll help build and scale the foundation that powers analytics, experimentation, and decision-making across the company. You’ll work on complex onchain data problems that few companies in crypto can tackle: joining a lean, high-impact team that directly drives product growth and user trust.

You’ll collaborate with Data Science, Product, and Engineering to design scalable data systems that bring together blockchain data, product analytics, and marketing integrations: enabling the entire company to move faster and with confidence.

Responsibilities

  • Architecture & Scale: Design and implement robust data architecture capable of handling 100s of TBs with 10x growth trajectory while maintaining performance and reliability

  • Data Quality Leadership: Drive data quality initiatives across the organization, implementing observability and monitoring solutions to ensure data accuracy, freshness, and reliability

  • Data Modeling Excellence: Lead sophisticated data modeling efforts to support exponential business growth, ensuring scalability and performance

  • Experimentation Infrastructure: Build and scale A/B testing frameworks to enable data-driven decision making across the organization

  • Cross-functional Partnership: Collaborate with stakeholders to translate complex business requirements into scalable data solutions

  • Technical Leadership: Mentor teams on data best practices and drive adoption of data-driven methodologies

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of extensive experience building and scaling data infrastructure in high-growth environments

  • Proven experience in startup environments with track record of wearing multiple hats and driving initiatives independently

  • Deep expertise in modern data stack tools, particularly Snowflake and dbt

  • Strong background in data modeling, schema design, and data architecture at scale

  • Demonstrated experience implementing data quality frameworks and observability solutions

  • Experience building and scaling experimentation (A/B testing) infrastructure

  • Expert-level SQL skills and proficiency in Python

  • Track record of successfully managing data infrastructure during periods of explosive growth

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with our tech stack: Snowflake, dbt, Rudderstack, Sigma Computing, Metaplane, Eppo

  • Experience with blockchain or cryptocurrencies

  • History of improving dashboard performance and query optimization at scale

  • Experience implementing data cataloging and metadata management solutions

This ideal candidate will be a seasoned data professional who can architect solutions for our next phase of growth while maintaining the highest standards of data quality and performance, thriving in a lean two-person data team where resourcefulness and ability to prioritize high-impact work is essential.

Role Description

Security is core to Phantom’s product and the trust millions of users place in us. We’re building an AI-native security team that aggressively uses AI to expand the speed, depth, and reach of our work—from code review and threat modeling to vulnerability discovery and security automation. We’re looking for strong security engineers with high agency who can identify the risks that matter, build practical solutions, and take ownership from initial discovery through verified remediation.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role spanning architecture, source code, testing, and production systems across Phantom’s mobile, web, and backend products. You’ll work directly with engineering and product teams, lead complex security initiatives, and build capabilities that scale across the company. At the Staff level, you’ll set technical direction and raise the bar for how Phantom designs, builds, and ships secure products.

This role is fully remote and open to candidates based in the US, UK and Canada.

Responsibilities

  • Product Security Ownership: Partner with engineering teams to identify and address security risks across Phantom’s mobile applications, web products, APIs, and backend services.

  • Architecture and Threat Modeling: Lead security reviews for new products and major architectural changes, with particular attention to authorization boundaries, sensitive data, transaction integrity, key material, and third-party integrations.

  • Secure Product Development: Embed practical security controls into the software development lifecycle, from design and implementation through testing, release, and production operation.

  • Code Review and Security Testing: Perform AI assisted security code reviews and targeted testing of high-risk features. Build repeatable approaches that help find vulnerabilities before they reach production.

  • Security Tooling: Develop and improve tooling that gives engineers fast, actionable security feedback without creating unnecessary friction. Use automation and AI-assisted workflows where they materially improve coverage or speed.

  • Software Supply Chain Security: Harden CI/CD, build, and release systems against supply chain threats, including dependency risk, secrets exposure, build provenance, artifact integrity, and compromised developer or automation workflows.

  • Vulnerability Management: Triage findings from internal testing, researchers, bug bounty submissions, and third-party assessments. Work with owners to determine real-world impact and drive issues through verified remediation.

  • Incident Response: Support the investigation of product security incidents and suspicious activity. Turn lessons from incidents into durable improvements to product architecture, detection, and engineering standards.

  • Technical Leadership: Establish product security patterns and expectations across engineering. At the Staff level, lead ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives and influence architecture beyond any single product team.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in product security, application security, security engineering, or software engineering, including experience operating at a senior or staff level.

  • Strong understanding of web, mobile, API, and distributed-system security, including authentication, authorization, session management, cryptography, and common vulnerability classes.

  • Hands-on experience building or applying AI-assisted security tooling to test applications and APIs, combining automated analysis with source-code review and manual validation.

  • Demonstrated ability to review production code in one or more languages such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Python and Go.

  • Experience securing software supply chains and CI/CD systems, including dependencies, build infrastructure, secrets, artifacts, signing, and release integrity.

  • Experience threat modeling complex products and translating security risks into concrete engineering requirements.

  • Strong judgment when evaluating exploitability, business impact, and appropriate remediation.

  • Track record of partnering effectively with engineering and product teams while maintaining a high security bar.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical risk to both engineers and non-security stakeholders.

Nice To Haves

  • Experience securing consumer financial products, wallets, payments, or other systems where client integrity and transaction safety are critical.

  • Familiarity with blockchain systems, smart-contract interactions, transaction simulation, signing workflows, or self-custodial wallet architecture.

  • Experience securing browser extensions or native mobile applications.

  • Experience building and integrating application-security tooling, static or dynamic analysis, security test infrastructure, or policy-as-code controls.

  • Familiarity with AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD systems, and cloud-native service architectures.

  • Experience working with bug bounty programs or coordinating external security assessments.

Platform security is foundational to protecting Phantom and the systems our users rely on. We’re hiring a Senior Platform Security Engineer to own and improve security across our AWS and Kubernetes environments. You’ll work directly with infrastructure and engineering teams to secure the control planes, identities, workloads, and deployment systems behind our most critical products.

We’re building an AI-native security team that aggressively uses AI to expand the speed, depth, and reach of our work. We’re looking for a strong security engineer with high agency who can identify the risks that matter, build practical controls, and own problems through verified remediation. This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable working in production systems, writing code and infrastructure, responding to incidents, and making security improvements without slowing down the teams building on the platform.

This role is fully remote; however, we’re only open to candidates based in the US and Canada.

Responsibilities

  • AWS Security: Own and improve security across Phantom’s multi-account AWS environment, including IAM, Identity Center, networking, compute, storage, secrets, logging, and organization-level guardrails.

  • Kubernetes Security: Secure production Kubernetes environments running on Amazon EKS, including cluster configuration, workload identity, RBAC, admission controls, network boundaries, secrets, container security, and tenant isolation.

  • Identity and Access: Design least-privilege access models for engineers, services, and automation. Build scoped, auditable, and time-bound access paths for sensitive production systems.

  • Mission-Critical Systems: Protect the infrastructure supporting products and services that handle sensitive data and high-value operations.

  • Cloud Security Architecture: Lead security design for new infrastructure, platform services, and major architectural changes.

  • Infrastructure and Policy as Code: Build reusable security controls using tools such as Pulumi, Terraform, Kubernetes policy engines, and automated configuration validation.

  • CI/CD and Supply Chain Security: Harden build, deployment, and release systems, including GitHub Actions, workload federation, build runners, dependencies, artifacts, signing, provenance, and access to production environments.

  • Security Automation: Build tools that identify and remediate cloud and Kubernetes risks at scale. Apply AI-assisted workflows where they materially improve analysis, coverage, or response speed.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner closely with Infrastructure, SRE, Developer Experience, and product engineering teams. Establish practical platform-security standards and help teams adopt them.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in platform security, cloud security, infrastructure security, security engineering, or a closely related engineering role.

  • Deep, hands-on experience securing production AWS environments. You understand IAM and resource policies, workload identity, network security, secrets management, logging, organization-level controls, and the ways these systems fail in practice.

  • Deep experience securing Kubernetes in production, preferably Amazon EKS, including RBAC, workload identity, admission policy, network policy, pod security, secrets, and cluster hardening.

  • Experience designing or securing mission-critical systems where compromise, excessive privilege, or loss of availability could have significant customer or business impact.

  • Strong understanding of identity, authorization, least privilege, isolation, and blast-radius reduction across both human and machine access.

  • Experience securing CI/CD and software supply chains, including GitHub Actions or similar systems, build runners, workload federation, artifacts, and production deployment paths.

  • Experience writing and reviewing infrastructure as code using Pulumi, Terraform, CloudFormation, or similar tools.

  • Ability to write production-quality code or automation in a language such as TypeScript, Python, Go, or Rust.

  • High agency and ownership. You can take an ambiguous platform-security problem from initial investigation through implementation and verified remediation.

  • Clear communication and a strong track record of partnering with infrastructure and engineering teams while maintaining a high security bar.

Nice To Haves

  • Experience with AWS Nitro Enclaves or other trusted execution environments, including attestation, isolation boundaries, secure key handling, and operational lifecycle management.

  • Experience securing financial, payments, wallet, custody, or other high-value transaction systems.

  • Familiarity with key-management infrastructure, AWS KMS, CloudHSM, cryptographic signing systems, or secrets-management platforms.

  • Experience operating or securing multi-region Kubernetes and AWS environments at significant scale.

  • Familiarity with service meshes and cloud-native networking technologies such as Istio, PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, or eBPF-based controls.

  • Experience with GitHub OIDC, Argo CD, Helm, Crossplane, or Kubernetes-based infrastructure delivery.

  • Experience using cloud-security and observability platforms such as Wiz, Datadog, GuardDuty, Security Hub, or CloudTrail.

  • Experience building policy-as-code, automated remediation, or security tooling used by a large engineering organization.

  • Familiarity with blockchain infrastructure or self-custodial wallet architecture.

Staff Backend Engineer who blends systems thinking with product pragmatism and a real passion for crypto. You’ll design, maintain, and evolve the backend services and APIs that connect Phantom Cash to blockchains. You understand both client-server architecture and blockchain protocols, and you know how to balance reliability, quality, and speed. You communicate clearly across pods, document rigorously, and elevate the engineering bar through execution and mentorship. Your work will make Phantom Cash feel dependable, seamless, and ready to scale.

  • Strong communicator and pragmatic problem solver - explains complexity simply, favors progress over perfection.

  • Node.js / NestJS at scale; event-driven design (queues, retries, idempotency).

  • REST API architecture: versioning, pagination, error models, authentication, rate-limiting.

  • Full-stack awareness: understands trade-offs of state management (client vs server) and latency budgets.

  • Smart-contract and protocol understanding: knows how on-chain programs interact with off-chain services.

  • Blockchain integration experience — Solana preferred, EVM acceptable.

  • Has shipped high-quality products in mature, high-bar engineering organizations.

As a Data Scientist at Phantom, you’ll help shape our consumer products through rigorous analysis, experimentation, and reliable data. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, and Growth to understand user behavior, identify opportunities, and guide product decisions.

  • Analyze user journeys, activation, engagement, retention, and monetization to identify opportunities and recommend product improvements.

  • Define and maintain product metrics, and partner with Engineering to improve instrumentation and validate the data behind them.

  • Build reusable analytical datasets and dbt models using SQL. Collaborate with Data Engineering on Snowflake, Dagster, and ETL pipelines to improve data quality and support analysis.

Kit is the email marketing platform experts choose to grow their audience, deepen their relationships, and build a business around the work they love. For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.

More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.

We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

The role

Kit is growing, and so are the legal complexities of our business. We're looking for a Senior Legal Counsel to help us navigate them with clarity, speed, and commercial savvy. You'll serve as in-house legal subject matter expert, partnering closely with the executive team to lead product legal strategy and execution—especially around privacy, data, AI and compliance, commercial contracts, customer security requirements, and scalable legal support for our teams. A key focus will be helping Kit respond to a growing volume of privacy questions—particularly as one of our newer products, Subscriber Signals, evolves by building practical, repeatable systems that provide timely and consistent guidance at scale.

You'll help shape the legal backbone of a fast-moving tech company with multiple revenue streams—including SaaS, digital commerce, paid reccomendations, and advertising—and a rapidly growing platform for creators. To advise the business effectively, you'll develop a deep understanding of Kit, SparkLoop, Subscriber Signals, and how creators get value from our connected ecosystem of apps and tools. You'll be at the center of complex, cross-functional problems where product, business, and legal strategy meet—all in service of helping creators build more valuable businesses.

 

Your support system

You'll report to our Chief Operating Officer, Brian Bevel, and partner regularly with leaders across product, sales, finance, and people operations. You'll own our core legal work in-house, reduce the need for outside counsel, and know when specialized outside counsel is truly needed.

 

What you'll do

  • First week: Get up to speed on our business model, current goals, and products. Learn about the product, SparkLoop, Subscriber Signals, and how creators get value from our connected ecosystem of apps and tools. Meet key internal stakeholders and our external counsel. Review our most common legal agreements, privacy questions, and customer security requests to assess where we have risk, opportunity, ambiguity, or recurring work that can be handled more efficiently.

  • First month: Get your arms around active data processing, privacy, AI, and other legal initiatives, and build a "what's on deck" view of upcoming legal needs. Map the recurring privacy support questions arising across Kit—particularly around Subscriber Signals, and begin designing a scalable intake, guidance, and escalation system. Partner with Sales, Sponsorships, Security, Product, and Engineering to move faster without cutting corners. Take ownership of GDPR and data compliance vetting and establish a clear process for responding to customer security questionnaires.

  • First six months: You’re the go-to partner for legal considerations across the business, particularly for our product, engineering, security, and GTM teams. Build scalable systems—such as playbooks, templates, intake processes, and self-service guidance—for answering recurring privacy, data-use, and compliance questions. Partner throughout the product lifecycle on initiatives and feature releases, with particular attention to Subscriber Signals and our connected ecosystem of products. Prioritize our biggest legal risks, reduce unnecessary reliance on outside counsel, and streamline legal workflows to increase speed, confidence, and self-service.

  • First year: Help Kit operate at a higher level of legal maturity across privacy, compliance, product counsel, commercial contracts, and security support. Establish durable systems that allow teams to answer common questions independently while escalating higher-risk matters appropriately. Help us treat privacy, data, and compliance as strategic enablers—not just boxes to check—and significantly reduce our reliance on outside counsel for work we can handle effectively in-house.

 
 

What will S.E.T. you up for success

 

Skills

  • Deep expertise in data, compliance, and product—this is where you'll spend most of your time.

  • Strong ability to navigate U.S. and European data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA), including familiarity with data controller vs. processor distinctions and how they shape vendor and product decisions.

  • Ability to translate privacy and compliance requirements into scalable playbooks, templates, intake processes, and self-service guidance

  • Experience supporting customer security questionnaires and partnering effectively with security, sales, product, and engineering teams

  • Familiarity with SOC 2 Type II and the legal, privacy, and customer requirements associated with it, even if you haven't directly owned a certification process

  • Understanding of intellectual property law, especially related to brand, content, and software

  • Understanding of commercial contracts—you'll become the go-to person for these at Kit.

  • Clear communicator and trusted advisor—able to simplify complexity and help others make informed decisions

Experiences

  • Experience as in-house counsel at a tech company or serving a tech portfolio at a top-tier firm that's well-known for their work with startups (e.g., Fenwick & West, Cooley)

  • J.D. from an accredited law school in the United States

  • Active member in good standing of a State Bar Association

Traits

  • Strategic thinker who sees legal as a lever, not a blocker

  • Deeply curious and business-oriented—you start by understanding the goals, then explore the smartest paths to get there.

  • Collaborative partner who can navigate conflict productively

  • Deep belief that creator success is our success—you consider both Kit and our customers in every recommendation

  • A "how might we" problem-solver who finds creative, business-aligned paths through legal challenges

 

What won't set you up for success

  • Needing a team of in-house peers or co-counsel to pressure-test every decision—you'll be our sole in-house legal expert, with outside counsel available as needed

  • A strongly risk-averse or "no-before-yes" mindset—we need you to help us move, not just stop us from tripping

  • Thinking in a legal vacuum—if you're not factoring in our goals, numbers, or creators, your advice won't land

  • Struggling with speed or ownership—if you prefer long timelines or wait to be told what to do, this won't be the right environment. We move quickly and expect people to take initiative, spot problems, and drive solutions.

 

Working hours and location

We're 100% remote with team members across the globe. For this role, we're looking for someone located in the United States.

The infrastructure supports creators who depend on Kit to reach their audiences and earn a living. When it's healthy, nobody notices. That's the job.

This is a full-time Individual Contributor role for an experienced infrastructure engineer who likes owning production systems end to end, takes on-call seriously, leans into automation and enjoys making other people's work easier.

 

Your support system

You'll report to Mojtaba Hosseini, VP of Engineering at Kit. Day to day, you'll work most closely with Kris Hamoud and Ivan Mora Perez.

You'll also partner with product engineers across Kit, and with teams outside engineering who rely on infrastructure to get their work done. Once you're ramped up, you'll join a three-person on-call rotation, which works out to roughly one week in three.

 

What you'll do

  • First Week: Get access to our AWS accounts, Kubernetes clusters, monitoring, and CI/CD pipelines. Read through our runbooks and architecture docs. Take part in Get To Know Yous (GTKYs) with Kris, Ivan, and the engineering teams you'll support.

  • First Month: Pick up day-to-day infrastructure support requests and start working through them with Kris and Ivan as backup. Ship your first improvement, such as a version upgrade or a fix to a gap in monitoring. Shadow on-call shifts. Write down what you learn along the way, especially the parts that only lived in someone's head or those that can be automated or improved.

  • First Six Months: Own core infrastructure areas end to end: databases, Kubernetes, version upgrades, and platform tooling. Take your full share of on-call, which you'll start by the end of your first quarter. Become the go-to person for day-to-day infrastructure questions. Find one recurring source of pages and make it go away. Ship a first paved path, such as a sandbox environment where AI agents or non-engineers can safely build and test changes.

  • First Year: You're the primary owner of a large part of Kit's core infrastructure, and you lead projects in it without needing direction. Uptime stays at 99.9% or better, page volume is down, and you've found real cost savings. Your paved paths are in regular use by engineers, non-engineers, and AI agents. You've built observability good enough for AI agents to handle some on-call load. You've documented your decisions so others can build on your work.

 
 

What will S.E.T. you up for success

 

Skills

  • Running production infrastructure on AWS at scale, including managed relational databases, networking, and load balancing

  • Operating Kubernetes in production: upgrades, capacity planning, and troubleshooting

  • Managing infrastructure as code and maintaining CI/CD pipelines that engineers trust

  • Building monitoring and alerting that catches real problems early and doesn't page people for noise

  • Diagnosing complex, multi-service incidents calmly, then fixing the underlying cause

  • Cutting cloud costs through right-sizing and reserved capacity without hurting reliability

  • Writing clear runbooks, docs, and decision write-ups

  • Nice to have: experience with Cloudflare, ephemeral or sandbox environments, or email sending infrastructure

Experiences

  • Around 7 or more years in infrastructure, platform, DevOps, or SRE roles

  • Owning production infrastructure for a product where downtime costs customers money

  • Carrying a pager for systems you owned, and making that on-call rotation quieter over time

  • Leading a major upgrade or migration, such as a database or Kubernetes version upgrade, with little or no customer impact

  • Building self-service tooling or paved paths that other engineers actually adopted

  • Working on a small infrastructure team where you couldn't hand problems off to a specialist

Traits

  • You own what you run. You spot infrastructure debt and fix it without waiting to be asked, and you follow through until it's done.

  • You build quality into the work. Upgrades have rollback plans, maintenance windows are planned around customers, and "good enough" is a decision, not a default.

  • You leverage AI effectively. AI helps you increase quality and velocity where it matters most. You know when to delegate and when to dive in, while holding accountability.

  • You make work easier for everyone else. You'd rather build a tool or write a guide once than answer the same question ten times.

  • You teach what you know. You write things down so the next person, or the next AI agent, can build on your work.

  • You work in public. You share context and tradeoffs openly, including during incidents and when things go wrong.

  • You use AI thoughtfully. It's part of how you work, and you help others adopt it without creating new risks.

  • You remember who's on the other end. An outage means a creator's launch email doesn't go out, and that shapes how you prioritize.

  • Wanting a well-defined backlog handed to you each week. Here, you'll find much of the work yourself and set priorities with Kris.

  • You are skeptical of AI’s capabilities, or conversely use AI without good judgement and accountability.

  • Wanting mostly greenfield architecture. A lot of this work is running, upgrading, and improving systems that already exist.

  • Needing layers of approval before acting.

For coaches, YouTubers, authors, podcasters, and other creatives, there isn't a better marketing hub to rely on to grow audiences, automate email marketing, and sell digital products — all within one platform.

More importantly, there isn't a team more committed to helping creators earn a living. We're on a mission to help creators earn $1 billion using our creator marketing platform. We have always been 100% independent and 100% remote.

We are proud to have built a product that our customers love, and we look for people who have enthusiasm and belief in our mission, vision, and values to join our team. We're also embracing AI thoughtfully — both in how we build and how we hire to ensure our team is adaptable, innovative, and ready for what's next.

The role

Kit's content team is producing more video than ever — creator interviews, webinars, product demos, and a steady stream of organic social — and we need an editor and videographer who can keep pace without sacrificing quality. This is a part-time contract role, not full-time, but you'll sit on the content team, working directly from our raw footage and briefs rather than a detailed spec sheet.

Short-form is the priority, but you'll flex between quick social cuts and longer editorial pieces depending on what the week calls for. You should feel comfortable filming and editing for both

 

Your support system

You'll report to Cait Miller, Team Lead, Content Marketing, and work closely with our social and creator education content marketers, who you will partner with for filming, briefs, and priorities week to week. Your other main collaborators are: our Growth marketing lead on paid ad social cutdowns and our in-house Brand team to understand the brand standards of Kit.

 

What you'll do

  • Film

    • Join us in studio or on set as needed for original Kit content

    • Feel comfortable both with on-the-ground filming as well as set and event filming

    • Experience working with creators a plus

  • Short-form

    • Cut organic social content — Reels, talking-head videos, product clips, UGC, and more

    • Turn longer creator interviews and webinars into paid ad creative

  • Long-form

    • Edit case study and creator interview videos

    • Produce quick YouTube product and feature tutorials

    • Edit evergreen webinar recordings into polished, on-demand videos

    • Slice webinars, interviews, and existing footage into 2–5 minute mini-course lessons for YouTube or other platforms

What will S.E.T. you up for success

 

Skills

  • Strong command of a professional filming and editing tools (Adobe Premiere Pro preferred; familiarity with CapCut, Opus Clip, or Descript as needed)

  • Fast, clean editing on talking-head and interview footage — pacing, captions, and audio cleanup that doesn't need a re-do

  • An eye for turning long-form footage (interviews, webinars) into engaging short-form social cuts

  • Comfort applying brand guidelines — fonts, captions, colors — consistently across a high volume of videos

  • Strong eye for quality and polish — Has a high bar for craft and can catch small details in cuts, pacing, transitions, audio, and endings that can make a video feel unfinished or sloppy.

  • Ability to work within a brand system — Comfortable interpreting and consistently applying brand guidelines across typography, color, composition, motion, imagery, and overall visual language.

  • Strong design fundamentals — Understands core principles like hierarchy, composition, typography, spacing, and visual storytelling, and can apply them naturally in video.

  • Collaborative with Brand/Design — Comfortable partnering closely with designers and creative leadership, receiving feedback, and incorporating brand considerations throughout the editing process.

Experiences

  • 4+ years editing social-first video content, ideally for a brand, creator, or agency

  • Experience editing both short-form (Reels/TikTok/Shorts) and longer-form (YouTube, webinar, interview) content

  • Hands-on experience with recorded interviews, webinars, or talking-head footage — not just b-roll or UGC-only editing

  • Nice to have: experience editing course-style or educational video content

Traits

  • You're fast without cutting corners — this team is high-volume and needs an editor who won't become the bottleneck

  • You can take a rough idea or raw footage and make it genuinely engaging, without leaning on clickbait

  • You take feedback well and don't need heavy oversight once you know the brand

  • You're comfortable juggling several projects across short- and long-form at once

 

What won't set you up for success

  • Needing a detailed shot list or heavy direction before you can start cutting

  • Discomfort with fast turnarounds — some weeks call for same-week social turnaround

  • Preferring to specialize in only one format — this role moves between short- and long-form regularly

  • A style that leans on clickbait hooks or gimmicks over substance

While Kit operates as a fully remote organization, certain deliverables require on-location support, including filming original content, supporting studio and on-set productions, and capturing footage at in-person events. These activities will primarily take place in New York City, so we will give preference to candidates based in the NYC area who can provide on-site support as needed.

This is a 6-month part-time contract (25 hours/month), with the possibility of extension. The monthly retainer is $3,000–$5,000, based on experience.

  • Own platform pricing and packaging. Define the SKU architecture for Flow and its modules: what is in the platform, what is in each module, the tiers, bundles, and add-ons, and the pricing model behind each, from per-endpoint licensing to consumption-based metering for data and AI workloads. Set list prices, discount structures, and approval thresholds, and keep the price book coherent as the product grows.

  • Run the monetization lifecycle. Lead new-customer and installed-base transitions when packaging changes, including migration rules, promotions, and true-up policy. Run quarterly pricing reviews, and partner with Finance and Deal Desk on price realization, discounting, and the deal guidance the field works from.

  • Define the platform go-to-market strategy. Decide which segments, buyers, and use cases we lead with, where the platform is sold as one product and where a module leads, and how land, cross-sell, and expansion fit together. Own the written strategy and the metrics that show whether it is working.

  • Build the sales plays. Design the plays the field runs, from the first-call narrative and discovery questions to demo paths, proof-of-value criteria, objection handling, and the commercial structure of the offer. Pressure-test them in live deals and retire the ones that do not convert.

Maintain the competitive point of view across incumbent DLP suites, SSE and endpoint platforms, DSPM specialists, and AI security entrants: battlecards, win/loss analysis, and the positioning that lets a rep win head-to-head. Own the product positioning hierarchy, platform-level messaging, and the proof points behind it, and keep them consistent across sales decks, the website, analysts, and partners.

  • Enable the field. Own product enablement for Sales, Sales Engineering, and Customer Experience: launch enablement for every pricing, packaging, or positioning change, certification on the plays, and the reference content the field uses day to day. Measure adoption, not attendance.

  • Drive strategic partnerships. Set the partnership strategy for the platform: which alliance, cloud, and channel partners matter to how we go to market, what we sell with each, and how partner-sourced and partner-influenced deals fit the plays. Work with the ecosystem and integrations product manager on what gets built, and own the commercial and positioning side of each partnership.

  • Measure and report. Define the metrics for the function, including price realization, discount depth, new-SKU mix, attach and cross-sell rates, win rate by competitor, and play adoption, and report against them in business reviews and board materials.

Who you are

  • 10+ years in product management, including at least 3 in cybersecurity, with time in a role that owned pricing and packaging decisions rather than advised on them.

  • You have priced and packaged a multi-product platform: designed the SKU structure, set the list prices and discount rules, and run a packaging transition across an installed base without breaking renewals.

  • You have built sales plays that reps ran, and you can show the before and after on win rate or deal size.

  • You have owned competitive positioning in a crowded market and won deals head-to-head against larger incumbents.

  • You have briefed industry analysts and shaped how a category was defined, ideally in data security, DLP, DSPM, insider risk, or AI security.

  • You are fluent in the financial side of the job: pricing models, elasticity, ARR and ASP mechanics, consumption metering, and the spreadsheet model behind a pricing decision.

  • Technical enough to position the platform credibly with security architects and to tell the difference between a feature gap and a messaging gap.

  • You influence without authority. You can get Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Engineering to adopt a decision they did not make, and you leave executive meetings with a decision rather than a follow-up.

  • An exceptional writer and presenter: strategy documents, plays, battlecards, and board slides that people read and use.

  • You operate with urgency and judgment in a fast-moving environment, and you are comfortable making a pricing call before every input is in hand.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; MBA welcome but not required.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Worked as an outbound product manager or product line manager at a security vendor, or in a pricing and monetization role at a platform company.

  • Priced AI or agentic products, including token- or consumption-based models, and worked out how they sit alongside per-seat licensing.

  • Led the go-to-market side of a platform launch that consolidated several products into one.

  • Run, or been a primary contributor to, an analyst evaluation such as a Magic Quadrant, Wave, or MarketScape in a data security category.
